paragraphs: Friend, here's what Proverbs 11 is shouting from every verse: how you live is not a side dish, it's the whole batch. Solomon keeps putting two roads side by side, and he keeps showing that the road is the reward or the trouble. "The integrity of the upright guides them, but the perversity of the faithless destroys them" (Proverbs 11:3). The wicked don't need a rival to trip them, because they fall "by their own wickedness" (Proverbs 11:5).

So what does the wise road look like? Honest scales, because "an accurate weight is His delight" (Proverbs 11:1). Humility, because "with humility comes wisdom" (Proverbs 11:2). A mouth that builds up, because "a gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence" (Proverbs 11:13). And money held loosely, because "he who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will thrive like foliage" (Proverbs 11:28).

Now the part I keep staring at: "A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed" (Proverbs 11:25). God's math says the open hand ends up full. So baker, this week, tell the truth in the small deals, hold your tongue when the juicy news comes, and give something away. Because "he who wins souls is wise" (Proverbs 11:30), and a life like that is a tree somebody else gets to eat from.
